A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAD research. All 23 pages in each version, including figures, equations, tables and Appendices A–E, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment experiments, decoding analyses and model comparisons in Section 4 and Appendix B, plus generated-response case studies in Appendix D.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark scores, GPT-4 judgments, timing measurements and case studies.

M1.justification: The stated decoding rule in Equation 13 replaces the base-probability term with its logarithm and removes the outer exponential. The logarithm changes token scoring if the equations are followed literally, while bringing it closer to the existing multiplicative policy. The architecture and training objective remain unchanged; an implementation change or rerun is not documented.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the training sources in Table A1 and P-Soups/HelpSteer2 evaluation coverage. The predefined and customized preference combinations, including the friendly preferences in Appendix B.2, are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains MORLHF, MODPO, Personalized Soups, Rewarded Soups, RiC, Preference Prompting, MetaAligner, MOD and Args. The customized-preference comparisons likewise retain Preference Prompting and MetaAligner; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The written training and evaluation settings are unchanged. However, Figure 3 changes two PAD bar totals from approximately 52 and 54 to 50, and one MetaAligner total from approximately 48 to 50. Neither PDF explains whether these are plotting corrections or revisions to evaluated sample counts, leaving that protocol question unresolved.

E4.justification: The beta/k sensitivity analyses, decoding-strategy comparisons and three Appendix D case studies are retained. Figure 3's numerical revisions do not introduce a new analysis, robustness question or experimental control.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three runs for the decoding-strategy comparison in Section 4.3 and Table B3. No repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Figure 3 revises three plotted loss segments: PAD on Pre/Con/Cre decreases from about 10 to 8, PAD on Pre/Con/Fac from about 20 to 16, and MetaAligner on Pre/Inf/Fac increases from about 17 to 19. Win/tie segments and numerical entries in Tables 2, 3, B2 and B3 are unchanged. The revisions are unexplained.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 inserts log pi_LM into Equations 19–20, correcting the base-probability term when converting Equation 18's multiplicative expression into an additive score. Equation 13 receives the corresponding correction. Equation 12 only harmonizes weight indices; the generalization theorem and Appendix C.2 proof otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: personalization without additional policy training, a single personalized reward model, generalization to unseen preferences and transfer across base models. The title clarification does not change these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of hyperparameter sensitivity and cross-model reward mismatch remain unchanged. Both versions retain limitations concerning inference cost, explicitly simulated preferences and disagreement between reward models and GPT-4 judgments.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same data-pair construction, prompt templates, LoRA settings, hardware, training hyperparameters and baseline implementation instructions. Both versions promise future code/model availability without adding access information.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix E and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning, including the comparison with MOD as the closest approach.

P1.justification: The title adds 'of LLMs', and several punctuation, capitalization and labeling inconsistencies are corrected. The narrative, section order and appendix organization remain substantially identical.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves upward on page 9, changing surrounding text wrapping and the continuation on page 10. Figure 3 is revised but retains its axes, legend and chart structure. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The log-probability correction in Section 3.4 and Appendix C.1 repairs a specific algebraic mismatch with the existing multiplicative PAD policy, improving the written decoding specification. The gain is limited: Figure 1 still displays the old probability term, and Figure 3's loss-bar revisions lack explanation. The broader evidence and claims remain unchanged.
